speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your skin condition, so please describe the lesion you are concerned about: how long has it been there, what does it look like, and has it changed in size or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC).

I have noted your history of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penis and a similar one on your finger, along with your significant smoking history and immigration from an area where syphilis treatment was attempted without success. Given the "red flags" for malignancy such as non-healing ulcers and the specific locations involved, I need to confirm the diagnosis immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion.
REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of finger lesion.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of lesions.
